facts.text: The town’s name, Chincoteague, first appeared in U.S. Board on Geographic Names decisions in 1943, though the island’s Native name was Gingoteague.
Chincoteague hosts the historic Assateague Lighthouse and Captain Timothy Hill House, both listed on the National Register of Historic Places.
Each July, Chincoteague’s Saltwater Cowboys herd wild ponies across the Assateague Channel, then auction the foals the following day.
When the Antares rocket launches from nearby Wallops Flight Facility, Chincoteague sees a surge of tourists eager to watch the launch.
Chincoteague serves as the gateway to the Chincoteague National Wildlife Refuge on Assateague Island, home to the famed Virginia ponies.
In 1965, most of Assateague Island was preserved as Assateague Island National Seashore, protecting its natural landscape from development.
